description.narrative: Geared for a Bright Future will improve public services for an inclusive and gender-transformative TVET systemas a catalyst for equitable and inclusive economic growth in Vietnam. It focuses on the provinces of Hanoi, Hue,and Can Tho9 but has a national reach. The project's ultimate outcome is “Increased equality and enjoymentof rights to inclusiveness and gender responsiveness of TVET services for women with disabilities, ethnicminority women and their communities in Vietnam”. The project responds to local needs and priorities, benefitingaround 50,000 WWD, EMW and their communities. 530 staff (60% female) from WU, VFP, PVET, DVET,DOLISA, MOLISA, NA and other women-led social organizations will benefit from skills and knowledge trainingand technical support. To achieve the ultimate outcome, we will: increase equitable participation of WWD, EMWand communities in TVET services (1100) and increase inclusiveness and gender responsiveness of the TVETservices required for an environmentally sustainable, circular and climate-neutral economy in Vietnam (1200).The overarching assumption is that the core problem can be addressed by tackling both the demand (1100)and supply side (1200) of the TVET system to set the foundation for an inclusive and gender-transformativegovernance approach that meets the specific needs of EMW and WWD. Oxfam’s innovative inclusive andfeminist governance approaches will empower rights holders by emphasizing participation and voice of the mostmarginalized groups, whilst strengthening thecapacity and accountability of duty bearers to deliverinclusive andgender-responsive TVET services. In Oxfam’s experience, a systems approach with multi-stakeholdercollaboration can lead to changes in public and private sectors and the EMW and WWD so these vulnerablegroups gain employment and thrive in their careersin a green and circular economy. Geared for a Bright Futurewill build on and scale up Oxfam’s and partners’ successful citizen’s feedback mechanism developed ‘M-Score’,which improved the public administration and health sector in Vietnam by tackling both the demand (citizen) andthe supply (public administration offices and public hospitals) of the system. M-Score is a real-time, innovativedigitalized mechanism using smart surveys, artificialintelligence and apps to enable the most marginalized toinfluence public services governance. It will enable EMW and WWD to express their training needs and providefeedback and recommendations on the quality, relevance and effectiveness of TVET services.M-Score will alsoallow businesses to regularly update service providers (PVET and DOLISA) and service users (WWD and EMW)on the job trends and skills demands, allowing PVET to offer training courses tailor-made to the specific needsof EMW and WWD and relevant to employment opportunities. It also enables local/national government bodiesto monitor the relevance and effectiveness of TVET services and integrate learnings into better TVET policiesand practices. Moreover, M-Score strengthens the ability and motivation of EMW and PWDs to participate, raisetheir voice and access TVET services. The project contributes directly to indicators SDG 4.5 and 5.5; and FIAP’sindicators10. The initiative will be measured using Oxfam’s Feminist Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability andLearning Framework.1110 Increased ability and motivation of WWDs, EMW and their communities, to shape/influencegovernmental TVET policies and programs.Achieving Outcome 1110 assumes that WWDs, EMW and their communities will want to work on areas ofenvironmentally sustainable, circular and climate-neutral economy and that if they are supported with relevantknowledge, skills and tools, they will be able to shape/influence governmental TVET policies and programs. Italso assumes that social norms change activities can create the conditions so communities are motivated to8 Canadian Feminist International Assistance Policy areas 1,2,3,4 of gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls, promotion of human dignity, growth that workfor everyone, women's economic participation. The alignment to Indo-Pacific Strategy: (i) by strengthening multi-stakeholders partnership, including non-state organizations,(ii) promoting democratic spaces (iii) promoting digital innovations (iv) contributing to the CPTPP from a demand-driven skills and labor rights perspective. Safe migration,supported by qualified vocational training, contributes to peace and security.9 Selected based on: (i) a high percentage of EM and PWDs, who are facing challenges accessing public services, including e-services9; (ii) opportunities to leverage UNDPgovernance initiatives, using PAPI9 baseline on vertical accountability dimension in 20239; (iii) the presence of highly motivated TVET partners (state and non-state); and, (iv)demonstrated interest and cooperation from provincial authorities, required for project approval at sub-national levels.10 Number of individuals with an enhanced capacity to advance human rights; Number of institutions (national/local) with enhanced capacityto enable inclusive, responsiveand sustainable public service delivery.

participating-org.narrative: In Vietnam , Oxfam is one of the leading international, non -governmental organisation. Since 1955, Oxfam is active in Vietnam withhumanitarian interventions and started development work in the late 1980's. Today, Oxfam works in 26 provinces with people, governments and civil society to promote equality and well-being through social and economic change.
